text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - British stocks rose to a record closing high as a clutch of results from leading companies beat expectations and the Dow made a firm start. The FTSE 100 index closed 27.0 points higher at 3,932.6, surpassing its previous peak of 3,918.7 set August 28.

FRANKFURT - German equities ended floor trade marginally higher, with a mixed performance across the DAX index of German shares ahead of U.S. jobless claims data. The DAX 30-share index ended the session 3.52 points higher, at 2,570.32 on small turnover. In post-bourse trade the index was up 19.34 points at 2588.04.

PARIS - French stocks finished sharply up, with a shove from bank stocks after strong first-half results, healthy oil share performance and a tug from rising bonds in the wake of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic inflation data. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 27.31 points, or 1.34 percent, up at 2,065.37, while the CAC-40 futures contract closed 20 points up from Wednesday at 2,066.0.
ZURICH - Swiss shares recoiled from losses in the second half of the session after U.S. producer price data, a firming U.S. dollar and early Wall Street gains helped the market.

Trade was rangebound and generally lacking direction, dealers said. Dollar sensitive stocks were in demand while banks were mostly lower. Nestle first half-year figures due on Friday and U.S. CPI data were keeping investors on the sidelines. The All-Share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 5.52 points to 2,361.99.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed mostly lower, with participants cautious ahead of the settlement of September futures and options on Friday. Worries about the domestic economy and a lack of political measures to shore it up clouded the market, brokers said. The key 225-share Nikkei average closed off 127.11 points at 20,443.93.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended modestly higher, with Henderson Land's solid fiscal 1996 earnings and overnight gains on Wall Street unable to arouse enthusiasm in a selective market, analysts said. The Hang Seng index rose 15.36 points to 11,251.72.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended weaker on Thursday, weighed down by major resource issues as investors factored in recent declines and further anticipated falls for base metal prices. The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 9.7 points down at 2,236.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks closed up as a late rally spurred by futures trade in the industrials sector overcame a market initially hamstrung by a sickly-looking golds sector. A rush of futures business, as dealers settled positions ahead of the close-out of the September contract early next week, dragged the market out of its noon doldrums and created a healthy volume of upwards moving trade. The all-share index closed up 34.6 points at 6,814.6 as industrials put on 48.8 points to 8,040.7.
